items.title: Man City whistleblower set to lose protection amid fears for life
items.summary: Pinto has witness protection status removed His lawyers will appeal and say his situation is ‘critical’ Rui Pinto has revealed he is preparing to leave Portugal because he fears for his safety after being informed that his participation in the country’s witness protection programme has been terminated. The Football Leaks founder claimed he has received “multiple death threats” and is facing “the serious risk of an assassination attempt against me” after being informed of the decision by Portuguese authorities on Wednesday. That came two days after Manchester City were found guilty of 115 charges by the Premier League – an investigation that was prompted by Pinto’s leaks of thousands of private documents.

items.title: Etihad’s statements on funding appear to contradict Manchester City’s defence
items.summary: Airline denied links to Abu Dhabi government in 2015 FA confirms it has powers to take disciplinary action Manchester City’s defence in their appeal against the independent commission’s guilty verdict in more than 100 charges of financial rule breaches appears to be contradicted by previous statements made by their main sponsor, Etihad Airways, to the US government. A key element of City’s appeal, which was confirmed by the club on Friday, is understood to be based on their claim that commercial contracts, which the commission concluded were part-funded by their owner, were in fact paid for by the Abu Dhabi government.

items.title: Robbie Savage steps up to take Peterborough job: ‘All I want is a chance’
items.summary: Savage leaves Forest Green to take League One role ‘Excitement is the word I can use,’ say MacAnthony Robbie Savage has been confirmed as the new manager of League One strugglers Peterborough. Savage has left his role at National League side Forest Green Rovers and signed a long-term contract at Posh, who are currently second from bottom and sacked Luke Williams last month. His appointment marks his first Football League role since retiring as a player in 2011 , and Savage said he is relishing the opportunity to prove any doubters wrong.

items.title: Neco Williams fires revitalised Wales to fightback win against 10-man Norway

Was this just one of those games where the game’s deadliest finisher was stuck on the fringes or was it a case of 115 things occupying his mind ? Either way, this defeat proved a humbling experience.

items.title: Criminal or saviour? Rui Pinto abandoned by Portuguese authorities after Manchester City leaks
items.summary: Man whose leaks of private documents prompted the investigation into City has been advised not to return home, contact family members or visit crowded places More than a decade after Rui Pinto set up the Football Leaks website in a crusade triggered by the Fifa scandal in 2015, he finds himself in the middle of a growing storm. The former history student with trademark spiky hair who used to make extra cash selling books about the second world war has not held back with his statements on social media since Manchester City’s guilty verdict from an independent Premier League commission. The first targets for Pinto, whose leaks of private documents prompted first Uefa then the Premier League to investigate City’s financial affairs, were what he alleged were the club’s “cheating” executives for demonstrating “a complete lack of respect for th

items.title: Manchester City fans are right to feel angry – now they need to direct it at the owners | Will Unwin
items.summary: Success under the Abu Dhabi regime made supporters feel proud, but they can only really get those feelings back under new custodians Amid the hundreds of thousands of words written and spoken about Manchester City being found guilty of serious breaches of Premier League rules, maybe Roberto Mancini’s were the most poignant when he announced it was “not my concern” . He made millions from one of the “sham contracts” and enjoyed his success but his ties to the club started and ended there. Since he has gone there will have been little looking at what was left behind.

items.title: ‘Is there still a glass ceiling? Of course’: Kazim-Richards fights for breakthrough at Crawley
items.summary: Alongside his assistant, Julian Gray, rookie manager talks about the state of play for black coaches and trying to lift his club off the bottom of League Two Colin Kazim-Richards accepts the scale of the task of improving the situation at Crawley who sit bottom of League Two after seven games. But on the evidence of what he has seen, the head coach is sure better times lie ahead. On a late summer’s afternoon at Crawley’s training ground in Sussex, Kazim-Richards, alongside his assistant, Julian Gray, the pair arriving in March and managing to save the club from relegation to the National League on the final day, speaks of the challenges ahead and how the team’s league position tells only part of the story.

items.title: The Nations League is a welcome example of soccer done well
items.summary: The tournament was treated with skepticism when it was introduced in 2018, but it shows that sometimes administrators get things right Sign up for our free newsletter here England’s first game after the 2022 World Cup was a 2-1 win away over Italy. Their first game after the 2018 World Cup was a 2-1 defeat to Spain. Their first game after the 2014 World Cup was a 1-0 friendly win over Norway – and that was not the Norway of Erling Haaland, Martin Ødegaard and Antonio Nusa but of Joshua King, Håvard Nordtveit and Tarik Elyounoussi.
